film.title: Akron, Ohio: The Magnet in the Nose
film.description:
In August 1973 a fourteen-year-old from Boulder, Colorado won the All-American Soap Box Derby in Akron with an electromagnet hidden in the nose of his car. Two days later the title was gone. The car was built under the eye of his uncle, a ski boot millionaire, in a race where grown-ups had been building the cars for years, on a stage Chevrolet had just walked away from. The boy lost the title and a $7,500 scholarship. It is worth asking who the real cheater was.

Narrated by Matthew Hagan. Marcus Vance and Nick DeLuca are fictional AI anchors with AI voices. The narrator is real. The explainer animation is AI-generated and labeled on screen. The opening score is original.

Local history... and college basketball. See more at https://hardwoodbricks.com

Sources:
TIME, "American Notes: Et Tu, Junior? (Contd.)," September 10, 1973
EBSCO Research Starters, "Cheating Scandal Shocks Soap Box Derby"

Westword; DBusiness, "Pull of Gravity"
The Village Voice, November 16, 1999 (the reported $22,000)

reels.title: The magnet in the nose: Akron, Ohio, 1973
reels.text: An electromagnet in the nose, a battery in the tail, and a switch behind his head. How a fourteen-year-old's car won the 1973 Soap Box Derby. A minute from our new film, Akron, Ohio: The Magnet in the Nose.

reels.title: Who is the real cheater? Akron, Ohio, 1973
reels.text: A grown man spends twenty-two thousand dollars to win a children's race, and the only name that gets ruined is fourteen. A minute from our new film, Akron, Ohio: The Magnet in the Nose.
